tldr: Goal: 2-3 new Venturis, changed in bore shape only. The top two get printed and bench tested the week of Nov 30. They need consistent dosing on piped flow from 6 to 100+ L/min, must still dose at 6 L/min, and must not make handpump overflow worse.

Piped flow: the 3-D CFD of V1-V4 shows dose varying about 2x over 6-60 L/min. Extrapolated to 100 L/min the spread grows to 2.4-3.3x. V2 (16 mm) holds dose most evenly; V1 (14 mm) overdoses at high flow. In the 1-D estimate the best single throat is about 16.5-17 mm, with about 2.2x spread. That fits inside the 0.3-0.8 mg/L band at one needle setting (2.67x).

Handpump: bench V1 dosed 0.31-1.32 mg/L from 7 to 26 L/min, already inside the acceptable 0.1-1.5 band. The weak dose at low pump rates happens because the Venturi stops running full: air from the pump head reaches it. Two-phase CFD confirmed this.
Running now: round 1 of the 2-D screen. 15 shapes (throat 14-18 mm, outlet 20/23/26 mm) at 7 flows from 6 to 120 L/min.

stages.name: Round 1: 2-D shape screen
stages.detail: 15 shapes x 7 flows (6-120 L/min), Venturi only, same setup as the 54 earlier 2-D runs. Pipeline check: V1 at 30 L/min must reproduce the earlier result.

stages.name: Round 2: refine around the best
stages.detail: Finer throat steps, throat length, port position, inlet cone and diffuser angle, outlet contraction.

stages.name: 3-D confirmation
stages.detail: Top 2-4 shapes on the aligned mesh, on both reducers (long-radius; E-Sig + McMaster 1in NPT elbow), 6-120 L/min.

stages.name: Handpump check
stages.detail: Pulse model with the bore-top priming rule from the two-phase baseline, plus a two-phase run of the best shape if time allows.

stages.name: CAD for the bench
stages.detail: Top 2-3 as threaded parts (same format as V1-V4), water path probed end to end, bench sheet. Target: ready by Sun Nov 29.

targets: Dose consistent from 6 to 100+ L/min. Max/min <= 2.67 keeps one needle setting inside 0.3-0.8 mg/L; aim for about 2.2.
Must still dose at 6 L/min steady: clear port suction, and the outlet must run full.
Ideal 0.3-0.8 mg/L, acceptable 0.1-2.0, keep below 1.5 for taste. No overflow (+5.8 cm above the spout centre) in the working range.
Bore shape only: no flaps, valves, vents, risers or added parts. Body 125 mm max. 1in thread, injector port, its thread and fittings, and the needle valve unchanged.
Piped and handpump use the same hardware: rubber coupler, then reducer (long-radius, or E-Sig + 1in NPT elbow), then the Venturi hanging vertically with the outlet open to air.

Print and test the top two: pipe rig, then handpump at 10-20 L/min
Reprint the long-radius elbow from the rev3 zip (rev2 had a solid wall at the coupler flange)

timeline.title: New goal: flat dosing, Venturi shape only
timeline.text: New targets: consistent piped dosing from 6 to 100+ L/min, handpump dose within 0.1-1.5 mg/L, and the bore shape is the only thing that changes. The vent idea was dropped and its two-phase run stopped at 0.33 s. Reading the 3-D V1-V4 results as piped flow ranks V2 as the most consistent. Round 1 2-D screen set up.

timeline.title: Throat variants V12 / V11 / V10 / V11t (125 mm body)
timeline.text: 3-D, aligned mesh, long-radius reducer, 6-30 L/min, all converged. Narrower throats give more suction but overflow sooner. Handpump windows (primed, no overflow): V10 13.7-14.8, V11 17.3-18.7, V11t 18.8-20.4, V12 21.2-22.9, V1 29.3-31.7 L/min. No fixed throat can cover 10-20 L/min on the handpump: the level rises with flow squared, so the window spans at most about 1.08x.

timeline.title: Two-phase (VoF) handpump baseline
timeline.text: V1 on the long-radius reducer, 80 clicks/min (13.2 L/min). The pump head drains. Once the level drops below the top of the inlet bore (+2.2 cm), air runs along the bore into the Venturi and dose falls to about half its steady value. This is the cause of weak handpump dosing at low pump rates.

timeline.title: CAD rev3: blocked bore fixed
timeline.text: The long-radius elbow sent on Nov 22 had a 3 mm solid wall across the bore at the coupler flange. It is fixed in rev3, and every CAD change now gets a water-path probe of the exported file before it is sent.

timeline.title: Bench data vs pulse model
timeline.text: V1 on the long-radius reducer on the handpump: 0.31 mg/L at 6.9 L/min, 0.93 at 14, 1.32 at 19.5 and 26 L/min. The pulse model's priming rule was too lenient; the two-phase run later set the right one.

timeline.title: Threaded long-radius elbow + V1-V4
timeline.text: Straight-thread joint so the injector port always ends up on the same side; print coupons first.

timeline.title: Mesh alignment fix and 3/4in retrofit
timeline.text: A mesh plane offset that varies with geometry was found and corrected (aligned mesh). On V1 at 30 L/min it shifted port suction by 9-13%. The 3/4in long-radius elbow retrofit was also compared.

timeline.title: Stage 5b: 3-D assemblies
timeline.text: 11 complete assemblies (3/4in and 1in trains, E-Sig + elbow or long-radius reducer, current part, A, B, V1-V4) at 6-60 L/min. Finding: the upstream parts alone nearly overflow.

timeline.title: Stages 1-3b: 2-D Venturi CFD
timeline.text: 54 axisymmetric runs: current part, prototypes A/B, V1-V4, all converged. The current part overflows; V1-V4 hold far less water.

bench.note: V1 on the long-radius reducer, Nov 23. Handpump rows from the stroke count; 28 L/min is steady piped flow.

piped_chart.title: Piped flow: relative dose vs flow (3-D CFD, long-radius reducer)
piped_chart.note: Dose taken as port suction / flow (needle valve fixed, viscous feed), each design scaled to its own minimum. Flatter is better; 2.67 is the 0.3-0.8 mg/L band.

rows: Best of V1-V4 for piped; low handpump backup
Dropped: overflow inside the handpump range
designs.note: Spread = max/min dose over the flow range on piped flow (long-radius reducer). Overflow = steady flow at which the Afridev level reaches +5.8 cm. V2-V4 are still on the older (offset) mesh; finalists get aligned-mesh reruns.

findings: Dose consistency on piped flow is set by how port suction grows with flow. Suction = (water column below the port) + (throat term x Q^2). With the needle valve's viscous feed, dose is flattest when the column term is about Qmin x Qmax times the throat term. For 6-100 L/min that points to a throat around 16.5-17 mm.

At 6 L/min almost all the suction comes from the column below the port, so the outlet must run full there. In a 26 mm outlet at 6 L/min the water moves only about as fast as an air bubble rises, which is marginal. A slightly contracted outlet keeps it full, and it is part of round 1.

Handpump: a Venturi runs full only while the pump-head level is above the inlet bore top (+2.2 cm) and below overflow (+5.8 cm). The level rises with flow squared, so the shape sets where the window sits, not how wide it is. Expect some handpump dose drop at low pump rates; the target is to keep it within 0.1-1.5 mg/L.

V2/V3-size throats are too large for the handpump (little backup, weak low-flow suction). V1 is too small for wide-range piped flow (overdoses above ~40 L/min). The answer is likely in between, with the outlet shaped to keep the bottom full.
